title: Build a baseline and a hypothesis
summary: Choose what the pilot will prove and how the comparison works.
objectives: Choose what the pilot will prove and how the comparison works.
Apply proof-of-value hypothesis to the worked customer example and explain its limits.

questions.prompt: A five-day technical pilot produces correct reports. Which claim remains unproven?

options.text: That it will reduce company-wide scrap costs by a specific amount.
options.rationale: The pilot did not establish that downstream causal or financial outcome.

options.text: That the tested outputs can be compared with expected results.
options.rationale: Those outputs can provide narrow correctness evidence.

options.text: That the team ran a bounded test, if logs show it.
options.rationale: Execution records can establish the test itself.

questions.prompt: The current-state baseline is missing. What should the team do?

options.text: Invent an industry-average baseline and call it observed.
options.rationale: That mislabels an external assumption as customer evidence.

options.text: Declare all future differences caused by the platform.
options.rationale: Other conditions may explain a difference.

options.text: Collect it with a comparable measurement method.
options.rationale: A credible before/after argument needs a real basis.

cards.answer: A customer-relevant claim that a bounded test can support or challenge.
cards.explanation: It should be tied to a decision, not a feature checklist.

cards.answer: It prevents narrow technical evidence from implying broader business outcomes.
cards.explanation: A pilot can prove prerequisites without proving downstream savings.

cards.answer: Aligned definitions, population, measurement endpoints, and relevant workload conditions.
cards.explanation: A mismatched baseline weakens the conclusion.
